terms.grammar: preposition with the accusative; also an adverb
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.51: ad mare īnfrā oppidum exspectābat
Cic. Fam. 9.26.1: suprā mē Atticus, īnfrā Verrius
terms.comment: Lower than a thing, not under it: īnfrā oppidum, below the town. As an adverb, below, or later in a text.

terms.grammar: preposition with the accusative (with the ablative in verse); also an adverb
evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.20: quae suprā et subter
terms.comment: Rare but classical (Lewis & Short). For “under”, see under.

phrases.latin: in lectīcā cubāns ad mare īnfrā oppidum exspectābat
phrases.english: he was waiting, lying in a litter, by the sea below the town

phrases.latin: in superiōre parte nāvigāre tantum, īnfrā etiam natāre concessum
phrases.english: in the upper part one may only go by boat; below, swimming is allowed too

phrases.latin: per nūdam īnfrā glaciem fluentemque tābem liquēscentis nivis ingrediēbantur
phrases.english: they were walking over the bare ice below and the running slush of melting snow

phrases.latin: omnia haec, quae suprā et subter, ūnum esse
phrases.english: that all these things, above and below, are one

sources: Lewis & Short: infra · Lewis & Short: subter
